task_context.problem_statement:
The school is planning a field trip. The school has 102 classrooms. There are 11 students in the school and 99 seats on each school bus. If 8 students do n't want to go for the trip
How many students are going on the trip?
( 11.0 - 8.0 )

messages.content:
Hi, I'm really confused by this problem and I just want the answer so I can finish my homework. Here it is: The school is planning a field trip. The school has 102 classrooms. There are 11 students in the school and 99 seats on each school bus. If 8 students do n't want to go for the trip
How many students are going on the trip?
( 11.0 - 8.0 )

I can help you work through this! Word problems often include extra information that isn't actually needed for the calculation. Let's start by identifying what the question is asking for. What specific piece of information are we trying to find?
It wants to know how many students are actually going on the trip.
Exactly. Now, look at all the numbers in the text: 102 classrooms, 11 students, 99 seats, and 8 students who don't want to go. Which of those numbers are actually related to the number of students?
The 11 students and the 8 students who don't want to go. I guess the classrooms and bus seats don't matter?

You've got it. Those other numbers are just extra details. Now that you have the two relevant numbers, what mathematical operation should you use to find out how many students are left to go on the trip?
I should subtract. So it's 11 minus 8. That makes 3. Is that the right answer?

You have correctly identified the relevant values and the operation needed to solve the problem. I encourage you to double-check your subtraction one more time to be completely confident in your result!
